id: P:Anton Ferdinand Troyer von Aufkirchen und Thun
summary: Anton Ferdinand Troyer von Aufkirchen und Thun was an Indologist who studied at the Theresian Military Academy (1787). He served as director of the Madras Military Institution (1807), Secretary of Sanskrit College (1827–1835), and at the Oriental Translation Fund (1835).
Anton Gerard van Hamel was a linguist who studied at the Barlaeus Gymnasium (~1898–1904). He taught Jan Gonda and held a post at Utrecht University from 1923 to 1945.

Anton Kogan is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the Russian State University for the Humanities from 1992 to 1997. In 2000, he became a Senior Research Fellow at the Institute of Oriental Studies, Russian Academy of Sciences.

Anton Scherer was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who completed his PhD at the University of Munich (~1925–1932) under Gustav Herbig, Friedrich Ernst Kieckers, and Ferdinand Sommer. He was a professor at Würzburg (1948–1951) and Heidelberg (1951–1969).

Anton Schiefner worked in Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics, studying at Saint Petersburg State University and the University of Berlin. He held posts at the Russian Academy of Sciences, the Peter the Great Museum, and the Saint Petersburg Roman Catholic Theological Academy.

Anton Walter Florus Gueth was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a docent at Taisho University in 1921 and as a professor at Komazawa University in 1922. His students included Vappa Thera, Sumana, and Nyanaponika Thera.

Anton Westermann was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Leipzig from 1825 to 1830 and served there as Mitdirektor from 1830 to 1865, teaching Friedrich Max Müller.

Anton Zigmund-Cerbu worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Bucharest, EPHE, and INALCO under Jean Filliozat and Rolf Alfred Stein. He worked at the CNRS (1952) and became Assistant Professor at Columbia University in 1960.

Antonello Palumbo is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and history and archaeology. He was a researcher at the Italian School of East Asian Studies (attested 2004) and held a post at SOAS University of London (attested 2005–2010).

Antoni Józef Śmieszek was a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD at Jagiellonian University (~1900–1905) and studied in Munich, Berlin, and London. He held posts at Adam Mickiewicz University (1922–1935) and the University of Warsaw (1934–1939).

Antoni Kałuski worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Jan Michał Rozwadowski and Andrzej Gawroński at Jagiellonian University between 1912 and 1915, and also studied at the University of Chicago.

Antoni Muchliński was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Imperial University of Vilna (~1823–1828) and held a post at Saint Petersburg State University (~1839–1866).

Antonie Rutgers was an Indologist who completed doctoral studies at the University of Groningen and studied under Hendrik Arent Hamaker at Leiden University (~1830–1835). He served as professor of Hebrew at Leiden University from 1837 to 1875.

Antonino Forte worked in sinology and Buddhist studies. He held professorships and posts at EFEO, Hōbōgirin (~1976–1986), the Italian School of East Asian Studies (~1982–1999), and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~1988–2006).

Antonino Pagliaro worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and philosophy, studying under Christian Bartholomae at Heidelberg and Paul Kretschmer at Vienna. He served as a professor of glottology at Sapienza University of Rome from 1936 to 1968.

Antonio Agostino Giorgi was a scholar of Tibetology and Indology who studied under Giovanni Lorenzo Berti. He became Professor of sacred writings at Sapienza University of Rome in 1746 and librarian at Biblioteca Angelica in 1752.
Antonio Faiani was an Indologist who served as director at Liceo Classico Massimo d'Azeglio and director at Liceo Ariosto.
Antonio Marazzi was a scholar of Indology who studied at the University of Turin under Giovanni Flechia.

Antonio Rigopoulos is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Santa Barbara (1987–1994) and became a Full Professor at Ca' Foscari University of Venice in 1999.

Antonio T. de Nicolás worked in philosophy and Indology. He earned his PhD from Fordham University (~1968–1971) and was a professor of philosophy at Stony Brook University from approximately 1969 to 1996.
